title: Can more be done to help vulnerable households in Wales stay warm and healthy?
official: Can more be done to help vulnerable households in Wales stay warm and healthy? An observational linked-data study
summary:
Background and study aims
Living in a cold or damp home can affect people’s health and wellbeing. In Wales, the Welsh Government's Nest and Arbed schemes have provided home energy-efficiency improvements, such as insulation and heating improvements, to help people keep their homes warmer. This study aims to investigate whether these schemes are associated with improvements in health and changes in healthcare use. We will also examine which households have received support, identify groups that may have unmet need, and assess the economic costs and potential benefits of the schemes.

Who can participate?
This study will use routinely collected, de-identified administrative and healthcare data. No members of the public will be recruited directly to take part. The study will include people of all ages living in Wales who are represented within the linked datasets used for the research.

What does the study involve?
The study will use securely linked, de-identified information about households, homes, energy-efficiency improvements, energy use and healthcare. We will compare health and healthcare use before and after home energy-efficiency improvements provided through the Nest and Arbed schemes. We will also identify households that may have unmet need and assess the costs and potential benefits of the schemes. Members of the public, including people with lived experience of fuel poverty, will be involved throughout the project and will help interpret and communicate the findings.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
There are no direct benefits or risks to individuals because no one will be recruited to take part in the study. The research will use de-identified information that is already routinely collected and securely held within the Secure Anonymised Information Linkage (SAIL) Databank. The findings may help improve understanding of the health and economic impacts of home energy-efficiency schemes and inform future policy and practice.

Where is the study run from?
The study is being led by Public Health Wales NHS Trust, Cardiff, Wales. Analyses will be undertaken using data held within the Secure Anonymised Information Linkage (SAIL) Databank.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
The study is expected to begin in December 2026 and continue until November 2028.

Who is funding the study?
The study is funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR).

Who is the main contact?
Dr Liam Mahedy, liam.mahedy2@wales.nhs.uk

interventions.name:
This population-based observational study will use anonymised routinely collected records linked within the SAIL Databank Trusted Research Environment in Wales. No participants will be recruited directly for the linked-data analyses, and the research team will not allocate interventions.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Any age
 2. Resident in Wales during the relevant study period
 3. Valid linkage to the routinely collected administrative data required for the relevant analysis
 4. For the Arbed and Nest recipient cohorts, resident at a property receiving an Arbed or Nest home energy-efficiency intervention on the relevant intervention index date
 5. For the estimated unmet-need cohort, resident in a Welsh household meeting the operationalised scheme eligibility criteria but with no recorded Arbed or Nest intervention
Exclusion criteria:
1. Individuals without valid linkage to the routinely collected administrative data required for the relevant analysis
2. For Arbed and Nest recipient analyses, individuals who were not resident at the intervention property on the agreed intervention index date
3. For analyses of the administratively identified unmet-need cohort, individuals with missing information essential to determine the operational eligibility criteria
4. For specific longitudinal analyses, individuals without the required period of observable residence, GP registration or outcome-data coverage
